newsitem.title: UK: IRAQ'S SOMO PLANS 875,000 BPD KIRKUK TO END-AUGUST.
newsitem.headline: IRAQ'S SOMO PLANS 875,000 BPD KIRKUK TO END-AUGUST.

text.p: Iraqi State Oil Marketing Organisation (SOMO) has scheduled loadings totalling 17.515 million barrels of Kirkuk crude for the period August 12-31, industry sources familiar with operations at the Turkish pipeline outlet of Ceyhan said on Monday.
The loadings, in eighteen tankers, plan an average 875,000 barrels a day (bpd) from the terminal.
Traders said the preliminary list for Ceyhan liftings might well be added to over the next week or so.
"This is a preliminary list and more cargoes may get added," said one.
Iraqi Oil Minister Amir Rasheed said on Monday Baghdad planned on selling 30 million barrels by the end of month, a rate of 1.5 million bpd over 20 days.
Given the schedule for 875,000 bpd from Ceyhan, that would leave Iraq planning to move 625,000 bpd from its Gulf port of Mina al-Bakr.
That compares with just over 650,000 bpd during the first six months of oil-for-food exchange permitted by the United Nations.
Iraq has permission to sell $2 billion worth of crude in a second phase of oil exports over 180 days.
After a two-month delay Baghdad has just 25 days to try to reach an interim $1 billion target by September 5.
Iraq's first 2.1 million barrel shipment is set to sail from Ceyhan on Tuesday August 12 aboard the Arcadia on behalf of U.S. trading house Bayoil.
Rasheed said the tanker arrived at Ceyhan on Monday.
Companies then scheduled to load before the end of the month are: U.S. Coastal, French Total, Spain's Repsol, U.S. Chevron, Turkey's Tupras, Russia's Rosneft and Nafta and Italy's Agip.
Buyers for three cargoes still have to be announced.
